title.en: Historical Underpinnings: The Acts Beneath the Constitution
title.hi: ऐतिहासिक आधार: संविधान के नीचे के अधिनियम

sources.name: Constitution of India, Article 395 (Indian Kanoon)
sources.what: Repeal of the Indian Independence Act 1947 and the Government of India Act 1935 with amending enactments

sources.name: Constitution of India, Article 372 (Indian Kanoon)
sources.what: Existing laws continue until altered by a competent legislature; President's adaptation power limited to three years

sources.name: Constitution of India, Article 248 (Indian Kanoon)
sources.what: Residuary powers of legislation with Parliament

sources.name: Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha At Work, Chapter 1: Evolution, Powers and Position
sources.what: 1919 central legislature (Council of State 60, Legislative Assembly 145, President appointed by Governor-General); Indian Statutory Commission on restricted franchise; 1935 federal legislature numbers; federal scheme never came into operation; Union Constitution Committee under Nehru reported 21 July 1947; old machinery not a satisfactory basis

sources.name: All India Radio News (Prasar Bharati), Three new criminal laws come into force, 1 July 2024
sources.what: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in force from 1 July 2024

q.en: Under the Government of India Act 1919, how many chambers did the central legislature have?
q.hi: भारत शासन अधिनियम, उन्नीस सौ उन्नीस के तहत केंद्रीय विधानमंडल में कितने सदन थे?

why.en: It had the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly.
why.hi: इसमें काउंसिल ऑफ़ स्टेट और विधान सभा थे।

q.en: Which Article of the Constitution repeals the Government of India Act 1935?
q.hi: संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद भारत शासन अधिनियम, उन्नीस सौ पैंतीस को निरस्त करता है?

why.en: Article 395 repeals it with the Indian Independence Act 1947; Article 372 keeps other existing laws in force.
why.hi: अनुच्छेद तीन सौ पंचानवे इसे भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम के साथ निरस्त करता है; अनुच्छेद तीन सौ बहत्तर बाक़ी क़ानून लागू रखता है।

q.en: In the federation planned by the 1935 Act, who held residuary powers?
q.hi: उन्नीस सौ पैंतीस के एक्ट वाले संघ में अवशिष्ट शक्तियाँ किसके पास थीं?

why.en: The Governor-General held them; today Article 248 gives them to Parliament.
why.hi: ये गवर्नर-जनरल के पास थीं; आज अनुच्छेद दो सौ अड़तालीस इन्हें संसद को देता है।

factsToCheck: Charter Act 1833 making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, and residuary powers with the Governor-General under the 1935 Act, rest on UPSC's official answer keys as recorded in pyq.json (CSP 2023 Q50, CSP 2018 Q38); the key PDFs were not reopened today

Script says the three 2024 criminal laws took the place of the older criminal codes; the opened source confirms the laws and date but does not name the codes they replaced (IPC 1860, CrPC 1973, Indian Evidence Act 1872 not opened, so not named)
Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, Government of India Act 1858, Indian Councils Acts and dyarchy were left out: NCERT PDF would not load (TLS failure) and no other primary source was opened
notes: Whether the Constitution 'copied' the 1935 Act is taught as a matter of emphasis with both views. Recent example: new criminal laws in force 1 July 2024, linked to Article 372.
